{{Short description|American physicist (b. 1938)}}
{{BLP sources|date=October 2022}}
'''Eugene Hecht''' (born 2 December 1938 in [[New York City]]) is an American [[physicist]] and author of a standard textbook in [[optics]].

Hecht studied at [[New York University]] (B.S. in E.P. 1960), [[Rutgers University]] (M. Sc. 1963), [[Adelphi University]] (Ph.D. 1967). During his graduate study he worked at [[Radio Corporation of America]]. His pedagogical work began in 1970 with a publication on a mathematical description of [[polarization (waves)|polarization]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Hecht | first=Eugene | title=Note on an Operational Definition of the Stokes Parameters | journal=American Journal of Physics | publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT) | volume=38 | issue=9 | year=1970 | issn=0002-9505 | doi=10.1119/1.1976574 | pages=1156–1158| bibcode=1970AmJPh..38.1156H }}</ref> [[Adelphi University]] hired Hecht to teach and he became [[professor]] in 1978, from where he retired in 2021.

Hecht challenged the notion of [[potential energy]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Hecht | first=Eugene | title=An Historico-Critical Account of Potential Energy: Is PE Really Real? | journal=The Physics Teacher | publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT) | volume=41 | issue=8 | year=2003 | issn=0031-921X | doi=10.1119/1.1625210 | pages=486–493| bibcode=2003PhTea..41..486H }}</ref> The elusive nature of a universal definition of [[energy]] was argued by Hecht in a letter to the editor of ''[[The Physics Teacher]]'' in 2004.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Hecht | first=Eugene | title=Energy and Work | journal=The Physics Teacher | publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT) | volume=42 | issue=L2 | year=2004 | issn=0031-921X | doi=10.1119/1.1787752 | pages=L1–L3| bibcode=2004PhTea..42R...1H }}</ref> In 2006 he wrote "there is no really good definition of mass."<ref>{{cite journal | last=Hecht | first=Eugene | title=There Is No Really Good Definition of Mass | journal=The Physics Teacher | publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT) | volume=44 | issue=1 | year=2006 | issn=0031-921X | doi=10.1119/1.2150758 | pages=40–45| bibcode=2006PhTea..44...40H }}</ref> He has continued writing on the topic, with publications in 2011 and 2016.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Hecht |first=Eugene |year=2011 |title=On Defining Mass |journal=The Physics Teacher |publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT) |volume=49 |issue=1 |pages=40–44 |bibcode=2011PhTea..49...40H |doi=10.1119/1.3527755 |issn=0031-921X}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Hecht | first=Eugene | title=Relativity, potential energy, and mass | journal=European Journal of Physics | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=37 | issue=6 | date=2016-09-20 | issn=0143-0807 | doi=10.1088/0143-0807/37/6/065804 | article-number=065804| bibcode=2016EJPh...37f5804H }}</ref>

Eugene Hecht has also written on American ceramic artist [[George E. Ohr]] and is a founding member of the American Ceramic Arts Society.

==Books==
His first textbook ''Optics'' was authored in 1974 alongside Alfred Zajac, a colleague at Adelphi.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hecht | first1=E. | last2=Zajac | first2=A. | last3=Stavroudis | first3=Orestes | title=Optics | journal=Physics Today | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=28 | issue=2 | year=1975 | issn=0031-9228 | doi=10.1063/1.3068822 | pages=54–55| bibcode=1975PhT....28b..54H }}</ref> In 1975, Hecht wrote ''Theory and Problems of Optics'' for [[Schaum's Outlines]]. Hecht is the sole author of his 1998 third edition of ''Optics''.<ref>"Review: ''Optics'', Second edition, [[Sky & Telescope]] July 1988</ref> Other works include:
*Hecht, Eugene (1980). ''Physics in perspective''. Reading, Mass.: Addison-Wesley. {{ISBN|978-0-201-02830-0}}
*Hecht, Eugene (1998). ''Physics: algebra/trig'' (2nd ed.). Pacific Grove, Calif: Brooks/Cole. {{ISBN|978-0-534-26100-9}}
*Hecht, Eugene (2000). ''Physics: calculus'' (2nd ed.). Pacific Grove, CA: Brooks/Cole. {{ISBN|978-0-534-37350-4}}
*{{cite book |last=Hecht |first=Eugene |title=Optics |publisher=Pearson |date=2017 |isbn=978-0-13-397722-6 |edition=5th |oclc=938342235}}

[[Brooks/Cole]] published a review of ''Physics: calculus'' in 1996, in which reviewers "found something intriguing on every page."<ref>Amy J. Kolan & Amy E. Larsen (1997) "An introductory physics text that conveys the author's enthusiasm", [[Physics Today]] 50(4) 65 {{doi| 10.1063/1.881732}}</ref> Hecht contributed to a celebration of potter [[George Ohr]] after his workshop was consumed in fire.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Clark |first1=Garth |title=The Mad Potter of Biloxi: The Art & Life of George E. Ohr |last2=Ellison |first2=Robert A. |last3=Hecht |first3=Eugene |publisher=Abbeville Press |year=1989 |isbn=978-0-89659-927-7 |location=New York}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Hecht|first=Eugene|title=After the Fire: George Ohr, an American genius|year=1994|publisher=Arts and Crafts Quarterly Press|location=Lambertville, NJ|isbn=978-0-9637896-9-3}}</ref>
